comparator.sourceNotes: Full current2026–2027 BAS common compulsory cluster totals111EC, plus3EC conditional mathematics/statistics and12EC thesis=126commonEC. SpecA has18EC compulsory plus6EC restricted choice, selecting first listed YAS33406 independently of UCR fit.30genuine elective EC close180. Complete57B1common+3ECMathA-preparation choice=60B1, then42B2common+18SpecA=60B2; complete12B3common+6restricted+12thesis+30electives=60B3. YAS21303 is a continuous3EC portfolio concluded alongside thesis; YAS21400 and general/lab/fieldwork safety are additional0EC obligations, not omitted credit awards. Thesis formal intake requires102compulsory/restricted credits including all60B1; AdvancedStatistics and SkillsAcademy before or alongside thesis. Use current API module requirements;2025scheme and2020–2021guide are historical cross-checks, not controlling requirements. The original generic/misnamed components and42EC mixed elective/specialisation bucket are replaced with exact current modules and genuine30ECelectives.
components: UCR Functional Anatomy studies human anatomy. WUR’s Zoology additionally develops comparative vertebrate form, evolution/development, histology and animal practicals.
General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
Dilemmas in Animal Management and Care
UCR Neurobiology includes animal behaviour, welfare and comparative neural mechanisms. WUR adds dedicated ethological observation, Tinbergen’s questions and behavioural-data collection.
WUR requires practical animal handling, feeding and housing training plus an individual husbandry internship. The UCR classroom/laboratory courses do not supply this placement.
Normal organ-system regulation is shared. UCR focuses on human physiology; WUR includes comparative animal morphology, histology and physiological practicals.
Shared host-defence and inflammatory mechanisms are a partial correspondence. WUR additionally integrates animal housing/climate stress, immunology and thermoregulation.
Epidemiological risk/design/causality methods are shared; UCR studies human public health, while WUR integrates animal disease-control decisions and veterinary economics.
Biochemistry shares nutrient chemistry and energy metabolism. WUR adds animal-specific requirements, feed formulation/manufacture, chemical feed/faeces analysis and live-animal trials.
Skills Academy is a 3 EC continuous portfolio across all 3 years, concluding alongside the thesis. UCR’s PPD develops shared academic/reflection skills in Year 1; the structures differ.
Exploratory data preparation, visualisation and R scripting are shared. WUR additionally connects advanced statistical models and assumption checks to animal data and uses Excel.
This example selects Mathematics Applied: Introduction for VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; other educational backgrounds choose with the study adviser.
UCR Marine Biology studies ecosystems, fisheries/aquaculture and human impacts; it does not reproduce the cultivation physiology and practicals required by Aquaculture Biology.
Introduction to Business Economics, Management and Marketing
Role of Livestock in Future Food Systems
This example chooses Role of Livestock in Future Food Systems from the 6 EC restricted cluster. Fish/seafood sustainability or Companion Animals are alternatives, not added requirements.

WUR requires an individual 12 EC animal-sciences thesis with proposal, research, written report, presentation and defence. Formal intake requires 102 compulsory/restricted credits including all 60 first-year credits; Advanced Statistics and Skills Academy are taken before or alongside the thesis. Optional UCR 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.
The pathway retains 30 EC for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. No specific minor is added to the required courses shown here.

routeSelection.basis: No route named in normalized target. Current official programme and handbook list SpecialisationA first, independent of UCR fit. Within its6EC restricted choice use first listed Role of Livestock in Future Food Systems, not an invented optional package. alternatives.label: Animal-related biology, ecology & welfare
alternatives.labelReason: Combine animal diversity, evolution, ecology and comparative neurobiology with cellular biology, metabolism, physiology, immunity and evidence about disease. Use farming, life-cycle assessment, ethics and sustainability governance to examine animal welfare and animal–environment relationships. Human biomedical study contributes shared mechanisms without replacing species-specific husbandry.
alternatives.concept: Combine animal diversity, evolution, ecology and comparative neurobiology with cellular biology, metabolism, physiology, immunity and evidence about disease. Use farming, life-cycle assessment, ethics and sustainability governance to examine animal welfare and animal–environment relationships. Human biomedical study contributes shared mechanisms without replacing species-specific husbandry.
progression: Each course has its required gateway completed in an earlier term and every assigned offering is planned for the fixed Fall2026 cohort. The plans develop biological or ecological foundations before advanced applications. Cell biology precedes molecular pathology/genetics, physiology precedes pharmacology, empirical statistics precedes meta-analysis and introductory R data work precedes machine learning where selected.

alternatives.label: Molecular physiology, disease & research methods
alternatives.labelReason: Investigate the cellular, biochemical, physiological and immune mechanisms relevant to animal functioning and health. Retain evolution, ecology and comparative neurobiology while deepening human anatomy, pathology, pharmacology, laboratory work, quantitative analysis and research synthesis. Species-specific nutrition, breeding and veterinary practice remain outside this programme.

Species-specific nutrition, breeding and veterinary practice remain outside this programme.

alternatives.distinctness: A concept-driven change toward molecular/organ disease mechanisms, laboratory and quantitative evidence synthesis, retaining actual evolutionary/ecological and animal-neurobiology foundations. Pairwise differences: 7courses / 52.5EC against programme1.

alternatives.label: Animal ecology, sustainable farming & enterprise
alternatives.labelReason: Investigate animal populations and the environmental consequences of farming and aquaculture using biodiversity, evolution, ecology, marine biology, sustainable farming and life-cycle assessment. Combine ethics and governance with economics, enterprise, marketing and market research to assess management and innovation; this is not training in animal-feed manufacture or food processing.

Combine ethics and governance with economics, enterprise, marketing and market research to assess management and innovation; this is not training in animal-feed manufacture or food processing.

core: Animal biology, diversity, behaviour, functioning, health and welfare
Cellular, genetic, physiological, nutritional and immune mechanisms
Animal populations, ecology, husbandry, aquaculture and sustainable food systems
Animal-data analysis, mathematical modelling, statistics and independent research
Welfare, ethical responsibility and human–animal relationships
adjacent: Physiological functioning and infection/disease mechanisms; optional infectious-disease minor
Biodiversity and life histories, sustainable farming and agricultural enterprise
Optional Foods of Animal Origin minor
questions: How do physiology, genetics, nutrition and environment shape animal health and welfare?
How can farming and animal-management systems improve ecological and societal outcomes?
How can quantitative evidence and ethical argument guide animal-related decisions?

candidates.label: Foods of Animal Origin
candidates.reason: Official optional minor example gives eligible organising evidence. It is separately owned, not claimed as a food-processing/animal-product curriculum in the ecology/enterprise response. Three earlier candidates passed their sequential gates; a fourth is outside the maximum. Welfare/human–animal interests are already uniquely owned by the closest response, not duplicated as a new candidate.

trace: Cellular organisation, biomolecules, enzymes, energy metabolism, heredity and gene expression provide shared biological mechanisms underlying animal functioning. Scientific-paper analysis is actual work; farm-species handling and physiology practicals are not promised.

Actual animal invertebrate/vertebrate diversity, phylogeny, organism identification and microscopy place animals in the tree of life. Broad biodiversity is not a specialist vertebrate-dissection or domestic-animal production course.

Structured Python programming, collections, recursion, testing and debugging provide concrete research-computing tools for reproducible biological/ecological work; animal-specific data or software is not guaranteed.

Actual R data cleaning, joining, exploration, visualisation and research-project reporting supply relevant data-analysis methods. No specific animal dataset or full advanced statistical-model curriculum guaranteed.

Functions, calculus, differential equations and actual population-growth/predator–prey modelling directly support quantitative ecology and physiological models. Current detailed content is calculus/dynamics; do not infer a full linear-algebra sequence from the short description.

Direct comparative/evolutionary neurobiology, animal behaviour and welfare, enrichment, regulatory behaviour and3Rs ethical appraisal materially connect neural functioning to animal welfare. It does not reproduce the full ethological/Tinbergen practical sequence.

Actual habitat loss/fragmentation, overharvesting, endangered-species management and conservation-status analysis support animal-population protection and human impacts. No captive-breeding husbandry or rewilding placement is promised.

Enzymes, carbohydrate/lipid/protein chemistry and energy/nitrogen metabolism materially support the biological basis of nutrient use. Feed formulation/manufacture, animal requirements and broiler/fish trials are not covered.

Direct disease-frequency/risk measures, study design, bias/confounding, causality and outbreak reasoning contribute population-level health evidence. Human public-health projects do not supply veterinary-economic decision analysis.

Population/quantitative genetics, natural selection, adaptation, sexual reproduction, life histories and Tinbergen-based evolutionary analysis directly support animal diversity and evolution. Designing a livestock genetic-improvement programme is an additional specialist skill.

Actual environmental/social/health life-cycle assessment, circular resource use, cost/revenue analysis and product/process appraisal supply substantive sustainability methods for production systems. Animal-food supply chains are applications, not guaranteed course projects.

Cell membranes, signalling, trafficking, gene regulation, tissues and bioenergetics are substantial mechanisms of animal cell function; research-method appraisal complements experimental study without claiming this taught course is wet-lab training.

Actual microbial culture/identification, antibiotic susceptibility, ELISA, protein purification, PCR and DNA analysis provide molecular/host-pathogen experimental tools. No animal-handling internship or live-animal physiology practical inferred.

Direct conditions/resources, niches, competition, predation, population dynamics and food-web/energy models explain animal–environment relationships. R ecological modelling and a research poster provide actual quantitative inquiry.

Ethical theories, argument reconstruction and independent philosophical judgment directly support dilemmas about responsibility to animals; the course description explicitly includes animal rights. No animal-welfare measurement protocol is invented.

Homeostasis, endocrine/nervous regulation, respiration, digestion/metabolism, growth and reproduction give substantial shared mammalian functioning. Actual study is human physiology; species-specific adaptations, husbandry and WUR animal practicals are additional.

Inheritance, genetic variation, epigenetics, molecular diagnosis and tissue injury/inflammation support biological health/genetics mechanisms and research design. The human disease/genetic-treatment context does not implement livestock breeding-program optimisation.

Actual marine ecosystems, production, food webs, fisheries/aquaculture seminars and human impacts support aquatic-animal ecology. Cultivation-specific feeding, reproduction, energetics and fish-health practicals remain additional.

Probability, estimation, confidence intervals, testing and simulation supply rigorous inferential tools for animal/population evidence; does not replace all life-science advanced regression/ANOVA training.

Innate/adaptive immunity, immune evasion, mucosal defence, vaccination and inflammatory pathology give substantial host-defence mechanisms with actual flow-cytometry-data analysis. Animal housing/climate thermoregulation is a distinct missing focus.

Human organ-system pathophysiology and mechanistic clinical-case reasoning deepen how dysfunction follows physiology. This is a bounded complementary mechanism contribution, not veterinary diagnosis, farm-animal disease management or the additional inflammation-focused WUR course.

Actual animal husbandry, aquaculture, alternative proteins and comparative environmental appraisal of farming/innovation provide a substantial direct sustainable-production contribution. The literature project is not animal-feed manufacture or an animal-care placement.

Food governance, institutions, public goods/externalities, stakeholder power and policy evaluation give concrete tools for sustainable animal-production decisions. Actual project is a Zeeland issue, not necessarily livestock.

Chemical equilibrium, molecular interactions, thermodynamics, energy and physical modelling supply a bounded foundation for physiological/biochemical processes. Actual starch-polymer experiment is materials work, not feed processing or bio-organic stereochemistry.

Neural signalling, brain organisation, learning and behavioural/neuroscience evidence appraisal prepare advanced research synthesis and complement comparative neurobiology. Human psychology is not animal husbandry.
Actual multivariable regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures models, diagnostic checks and R analyses provide direct advanced empirical methods for health/biological research.

Pharmacodynamics/kinetics, antimicrobial action and immune/inflammatory drug mechanisms deepen infection/physiology research. Virtual quantitative experiments are not veterinary prescribing or livestock-treatment training.

Regression/classification, validation/resampling and predictor evaluation in R/Python develop analysis of complex biological/health data. A predictive model is not causal inference, and an animal-data project is not guaranteed.

Human skeletal/organ anatomy, imaging and three-dimensional structure–function reasoning deepen physiological mechanisms. This is a partial mammalian-anatomy relationship; comparative vertebrate development and WUR animal dissection/histology are missing.

Systematic reviews, risk-of-bias appraisal, effect sizes, R meta-analysis and moderator/heterogeneity analysis provide substantial research-synthesis methods. A taught group synthesis is not WUR individual original animal-data thesis work.

Supply/demand, consumer choice, production/costs and strategic interaction explain real resource and incentive constraints on farming businesses. Macroeconomic content is broader; veterinary economics is not inferred.

Measurement, sampling, surveys/experiments, inference/regression and R-based project design/data collection supply empirical methods for management and stakeholder evidence. Animal-specific measurement remains additional.

Business environments, finance/operations, customer needs and actual business-model/plan development supply concrete enterprise tools for sustainable farming innovation. No food/animal-sector venture or full agricultural business qualification is guaranteed.

The available description supports strategy from vision to implementation, responsible digital transformation and industry-case analysis of business models and social responsibility. These are fully considered management tools; no agriculture-specific case is invented.

Public goods/externalities, efficiency/equity and model-based public-policy analysis supply direct tools for evaluating environmental costs and collective decisions around farming. The course is broader than agricultural economics.

Marketing strategy, consumer psychology, responsible branding and primary/secondary consumer research contribute real tools for adoption and demand in sustainable food/enterprise systems. No animal-product marketing project is guaranteed.

The available description supports planning/conducting customer research, analysing results and presenting business recommendations. This provides substantive empirical enterprise inquiry; no unlisted method or food-sector placement is assumed.
blocks: Shared cell structure, membranes, signalling, gene regulation and bioenergetics. WUR includes its own cell/biochemical laboratory practicals; UCR’s Molecular Cell Biology emphasises molecular mechanisms and research appraisal.

Shared normal mammalian homeostasis, endocrine/nervous control and integrated organ-system function. UCR focuses on humans; WUR includes comparative animal morphology, histology and physiology practicals.

Shared biomolecular nutrient chemistry, enzyme function and energy/nitrogen metabolism. WUR additionally teaches animal-specific requirements, diet formulation/processing, feed analysis and live-animal trials.

Shared mammalian anatomical structure–function reasoning and study of skeletal/organ material. UCR studies human anatomy; WUR develops comparative vertebrate anatomy, evolution/development, histology and animal physiological practicals.

Shared innate/adaptive host defence, inflammation and disease-resistance mechanisms. WUR integrates environmental stress and animal thermoregulation; UCR includes host-pathogen mechanisms and flow-cytometry-data analysis.

Shared animal behaviour, evolutionary/neural mechanisms, welfare and ethical research appraisal. WUR additionally teaches a dedicated ethological/Tinbergen framework and collects/analyses behavioural observations.

Shared chemical equilibrium, molecular/energy principles and thermodynamics. UCR uses environmental/material contexts and does not reproduce the complete life-science buffer, kinetics and ATP-coupling sequence.

Shared ethical theory/argument and independent position on practical moral responsibility, including animal-rights applications at UCR. WUR specifically analyses animal management practices and their welfare/sustainability dilemmas.
No selected course integrates the full animal-sciences orientation across species, behaviour/ecology, production and health. Shared cellular/ecological contributions remain separately identified.
No selected course reproduces domestic-animal production biology, live-animal phenotype measurements, feeding/housing, lactation and comparative practical cases.
No adequate whole counterpart for bio-organic reactions, stereochemistry and natural-product structure/reactivity. Biochemistry is most strongly aligned to nutrient metabolism.
Required practical handling/feeding/housing training and individual animal-husbandry internship are not replaced by classroom biology or a community project.
Evolutionary and human genetic mechanisms do not reproduce designing and optimising livestock/companion-animal breeding programmes.
Marine ecology and aquaculture topics are relevant but do not reproduce aquatic-animal cultivation physiology, feeding/growth/reproduction and practicals.
General human reproductive anatomy/physiology does not reproduce farm/companion-species fertility cycles, management and reproductive technologies.
The additional animal-management/inflammation/metabolic/behavioural disorder sequence remains separate; shared host defence is aligned to Immunology and Thermoregulation.

Shared Mendelian, population/quantitative and evolutionary genetics, variation and selection. WUR additionally develops detailed molecular genetic problems and case exercises; UCR develops broader evolutionary history and Tinbergen analysis.

Shared environmental conditions/resources, population dynamics, predation, competition and food webs, with quantitative ecological modelling. WUR focuses on animals, ecological-requirement projects and wildlife observation.

Shared environmental/social appraisal of animal husbandry, aquaculture, alternative proteins and farming innovations. WUR specifically compares competing livestock-food-system narratives, planetary/human/animal health and feed–food/circularity dilemmas.

Shared sustainability assessment, production-system impacts and circular-resource reasoning. WUR integrates systems/linear-programming and qualitative methods in a livestock case; UCR develops product/process life-cycle assessment.
Shared business-environment analysis, marketing/finance/operations and an integrated business plan. WUR applies planning to a food-supply-chain enterprise; UCR develops a new-venture concept.
Population evidence, research methods & academic skills

Shared academic writing/presentation, personal goals, reflection and collaboration. UCR is a Year1 course with civic engagement; WUR’s3EC SkillsAcademy runs across all3years and concludes alongside the thesis.
Shared disease frequency, causal reasoning, epidemiological designs, risk and outbreak analysis. UCR is human public health; WUR adds animal-population disease control and economic decision methods.

Shared differentiation, integration, differential equations and mathematical modelling. UCR adds dynamic population/predator–prey modelling; the prior-preparation introduction and separate linear-algebra award remain distinct.

Shared statistical estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing, grounded in probability and simulation at UCR. WUR additionally develops simple applied regression for life-science data; the advanced-statistics award remains separate.
Shared exploratory analysis, data preparation/visualisation and R scripting/reporting. WUR connects advanced statistical-model building/checks specifically to animal data and also uses Excel.
Shared multiple regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures models, assumptions and R-based data interpretation. Applications and exact inferential scope differ.
No selected dedicated vectors/matrices/eigenvalues/linear-algebra course; current Mathematical Methods detailed content is calculus/dynamic modelling.
This prior-preparation-dependent3EC introduction remains separate; UCR Mathematical Methods is aligned once to the stronger applied-analysis component.

Required individual animal-sciences research, proposal, original data analysis, thesis, presentation and defence have no taught-course counterpart. Optional UCR independent research is a separate opportunity outside the24courses/180EC.
Genuine30EC minor/elective space has no specified subject counterpart.

selection.assessment: Three sequentially tested material related responses: animal-related biological/ecological mechanisms and welfare; molecular physiology/disease/evidence synthesis; animal ecology/farming/environmental assessment and enterprise. The unimplemented Foods of Animal Origin direction remains separately owned; no professional or disciplinary equivalence claimed.

notes.text: UCR can combine substantive animal-related ecology, evolution, comparative neurobiology, sustainable farming and shared biological mechanisms. Its biomedical courses largely study humans. WUR adds dedicated domestic-animal production biology, nutrition/feed practicals, breeding, fertility, aquaculture physiology, animal handling and husbandry internship, and a required animal-sciences thesis. These related UCR programmes do not reproduce that specialist sequence. Optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: WUR’s English-taught Animal Sciences bachelor studies domesticated and wild animals, from cells and physiological mechanisms to behaviour, welfare, ecology and sustainable production. Animal Management and Care emphasises animals in their environment and society, including nutrition, reproduction, housing and management.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines animal-related biology, ecology and welfare with shared biomedical mechanisms. The second deepens molecular physiology, disease and research methods; the third combines animal ecology and sustainable farming with environmental assessment, governance and enterprise. WUR provides more specialised animal nutrition, breeding, fertility, aquaculture physiology and hands-on husbandry. Human biomedical study contributes shared mechanisms and does not replace species-specific training. WUR’s individual thesis is required; UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits.
